newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Prague PX50 falls 2.6 points on SPT losses.
newsitem.headline: Prague PX50 falls 2.6 points on SPT losses.

text.p: Shares in Czech SPT Telecom a.s. gave back on Wednesday some of the strong gains it posted one day earlier, putting the Prague Stock Exchange's PX50 index into negative territory for the session.
SPT, the bourse's most highly-capitalised issue, lost 57 crowns after gaining 177 on Tuesday to close the Wednesday session at 3,600, while the PX50 lost 2.6 points or 0.51 percent to close at 504.9.
Analysts cite the uncertainty surrounding SPT losses due to the massive flooding in the eastern part of the country as a reason for the stock's recent volatility.

"With a view to the current nervousness of investors connected to the possible losses of (SPT) from the flooding it is possible to imagine the stock falling to 3,200," said Petr Vins, a broker at Stratego Invest.
SPT has estimated that lost service and damage to infrastructure would cost the company "hundreds of millions" of crowns, but SPT officials say the losses are manageable for such a large company.

Elsewhere on the bourse, CEZ power made a late surge at the end of the real-time session to close eight crowns higher at 918, while the most-liquid banking issue, Komercni Banka, was unchanged at 1,740.
Overall volume in automated and direct trading was 615 million crowns as 502,864 shares changed hands on the PSE session.
